name: Grades Reviews
author: Grades.com

sections.description:
Grades Reviews reads the public reviews API of Grades.com and prints your customer reviews in your own theme’s design. For the reviews, rating and showcase shortcodes everything happens on your server: the plugin fetches the reviews, caches them, and writes plain HTML, with no JavaScript, no iframe and no request from your visitors’ browsers. Only the optional review widgets ([grades_widget]) load from Grades.com in the visitor’s browser (see External services).

  • [grades_reviews] shows a grid or list of reviews, filtered by rating and review site.
  • [grades_rating] prints “4.8 out of 5 from 1,353 reviews”.
  • [grades_showcase showcase="..."] shows your Review Showcase: your reviews, picked by rules you set on Grades.com (or count, min_rating, topic, sites, max_age_days, language attributes). Reviews are never shortened, and the block links to all your reviews.
  • [grades_widget preset="strip|carousel|grid|..."], the “Grades Review Widget” block and the Elementor widget show the Grades.com review widgets (they load from Grades.com, see External services).
  • Fitting your site on [grades_widget]: background="transparent" (your colored section shows between the review cards), font="inter|montserrat|open-sans|roboto" (fonts bundled with Grades.com, nothing loads from a third party; or inherit, system, serif), and for the floating badge, pop-ups and tab offset_bottom, offset_side and offset_bottom_mobile (0-200 px, e.g. offset_bottom_mobile="80" above a sticky bar on phones).
  • min_cards="3" on [grades_widget] hides the widget while fewer than 3 reviews qualify (1-10), for example with min_rating="4" on a city page; hide_if_empty then hides its section too.
  • A classic widget for sidebars (no block editor needed).
  • A server-rendered block for block themes (see the FAQ for the editor caveat).
  • With Elementor: a “Grades.com Reviews” widget in the Elementor panel (drag it onto the page, pick the layout and options in its settings, see it live in the editor).
  • Several locations, one key: with a key created on your headquarters business, locations="all" (or the ids of the offices a page is about) works on every shortcode, block, Elementor widget and the JSON-LD, with the true combined rating of exactly those locations.
  • Optional JSON-LD aggregateRating for your business (rating and count only, never review text), printed once in the page head; it can join your SEO plugin’s entity by @id.
  • Responses are cached with transients; a failing API never slows the page down for more than 5 seconds and is not retried for 2 minutes.
  • Review text and names are escaped, stars carry a text alternative, and a theme can replace the review markup with grades-reviews/review.php.

You need a Grades.com account and a publishable key (gk_pub_...). Create one in the Grades dashboard under your location’s keys.

WooCommerce review requests (1.6.0)

With WooCommerce active, WooCommerce > Grades.com reviews sends your Grades.com review request to the customer after an order is completed. Off until you switch it on.

  • Ask when an order is Completed (default) or Processing, after a delay you choose (default 7 days), through WooCommerce’s Action Scheduler.
  • One request per order, and at most one per customer every 90 days by default (Grades.com applies its own limit too and never asks again someone who already left a review after a request).
  • At send time, refunded, canceled or failed orders are skipped; optionally free orders too.
  • Customers who opted out with Grades.com are never asked. If your checkout or newsletter plugin stores marketing consent in an order or customer field, name it and the plugin respects it.
  • Every customer gets the same request: the plugin never looks at products, order value (beyond the optional free-order switch) or how happy a customer seems, asks for no rating first and offers no reward. That keeps you within Google’s review policy and the FTC rule on consumer reviews (16 CFR 465).
  • A note on each order (queued, sent, skipped and why), a log of the last 50 events with masked emails, and an optional “Send review request now” order action (off by default).
  • Works on every paid Grades.com plan (on Starter up to 50 review requests a month, by email, without reminders) and needs a secret API key (gk_live_..., scopes reviews:read, reviews:write, companies:read), created at https://my.grades.com/connect?connect=woocommerce. The key is stored with autoload off, sent only from your server and never shown again.
  • HPOS (custom order tables) compatible; orders are read and written through the WooCommerce order API.

Shortcode: reviews

[grades_reviews limit="6" min_rating="4" sources="google,yelp" sort="best" layout="grid" show_source="1" show_date="1"]
  • limit 1-50, default 6
  • min_rating 1-5, default from Settings
  • sources comma separated, default from Settings (empty = all)
  • sort newest (default) or best
  • layout grid (default) or list
  • show_source, show_date 1 or 0
  • max_chars characters shown before “Read more”, default 280
  • locations (a key created on a headquarters business) all or location ids, comma separated; default: the key’s own business
  • show_location 1 puts the office on each review (with locations)

Shortcode: rating

[grades_rating] or `[grades_rating sources="google" stars="0"]` or `[grades_rating locations="all"]`

Several locations on one site (1.11.0)

Create ONE publishable key on your headquarters (HQ) business at my.grades.com and paste it in Settings > Grades Reviews. Then:

  • Home page or reviews page: [grades_widget preset="carousel" locations="all"], [grades_rating locations="all"]: every location, with the true combined rating and count.
  • A city page: [grades_widget preset="grid" locations="<id>,<id>"] (the location ids are listed in the widget editor’s “Which reviews” step at my.grades.com), or a widget saved at my.grades.com with its own choice of locations: [grades_widget widget_id="<saved widget id>"].
  • A saved showcase of any of your locations works with the HQ key: [grades_showcase showcase="<id>"].
  • show_location="on" (widgets) or show_location="1" ([grades_reviews], [grades_showcase]) names the office on each review.

Without locations, [grades_reviews], [grades_rating], [grades_showcase] and the JSON-LD show the key’s own business (as before 1.11.0), while a widget on an HQ key shows all locations by default (as on Grades.com). If Grades.com refuses a value (a location that is not yours), administrators see a short note with the reason where the reviews would be; visitors see nothing.

Theme override

Create grades-reviews/review.php in your theme. It receives $review (author, rating, site (the review platform: google, yelp, facebook…), source (the same), source_label, text, excerpt, truncated, date, url, response_text, response_date; all text is plain, escape it when printing) and $args.

External services

This plugin calls the Grades.com public reviews API (https://app.grades.com/api/v1/public/reviews, /public/summary and /public/showcase; the base URL is configurable) from your web server to fetch your reviews and rating summary. It sends your publishable key (header X-Grades-Key), the filter values of the shortcode (limit, sort, minimum rating, sources, locations, and the showcase rules: showcase id, count, topic, text length, age, language) and a User-Agent containing the plugin version and your site URL. Nothing about your visitors is sent from your server.

The optional review widgets ([grades_widget], the “Grades Review Widget” block and the Elementor “Grades.com Reviews” widget) are loaded in your visitors’ browsers from Grades.com: the script https://app.grades.com/embed/widget.js, or a frame from https://app.grades.com/embed/widget/... with iframe="1" and in the editor preview. The page carries your publishable key and the widget options (layout, filters, colors, language, the locations of a headquarters key, a saved widget id). As with any web request, the visitor’s browser sends Grades.com its IP address, browser user agent and the page address (frames send only your site’s origin). The widget sets no cookie. Nothing loads from Grades.com in your visitors’ browsers unless you place a widget. Terms of use: https://www.grades.com/terms. Privacy policy: https://www.grades.com/privacy-policy.

With WooCommerce and the review requests switched on (WooCommerce > Grades.com reviews), the plugin also calls the authenticated Grades.com API v1 (https://app.grades.com/api/v1, same configurable base URL) from your web server with your secret key (header Authorization: Bearer): /me, /companies and /companies/{business}/review-requests/settings when you save the settings, press Test connection, or open that settings screen more than 10 minutes after the last check, and POST /companies/{business}/review-requests once per eligible order, when the request is due. For each order it sends the customer’s billing name and billing email, an order reference made of a hash of your site address and the order id, the consent source “woocommerce_order”, and the plugin version and site URL in the User-Agent. Grades.com then emails the customer your review request with an unsubscribe link. Nothing is sent for orders while the feature is off. Service: Grades.com, https://www.grades.com/integrations/wordpress. Terms of use: https://www.grades.com/terms. Privacy policy: https://www.grades.com/privacy-policy.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the grades-reviews folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or upload the zip under Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to Settings > Grades Reviews, paste your publishable key and save. The page shows “Connected to …” when the key works.
  4. Add [grades_reviews] to a page, or add the “Grades Reviews” widget to a sidebar.
  5. Optional, with WooCommerce: open WooCommerce > Grades.com reviews, paste a secret key, pick the business, press Test connection, then switch on review requests.
sections.faq:
My site has a strict Content-Security-Policy and the widgets do not show

Allow Grades.com for scripts and frames: script-src 'self' https://app.grades.com; frame-src https://app.grades.com (with iframe="1" only frame-src is needed). The widget brings its own styles and fonts inside its frame. The reviews, rating and showcase shortcodes are plain HTML from your server and need style-src 'unsafe-inline', as WordPress itself does.

Which customers get a WooCommerce review request?

Every customer whose order reaches the status you chose, unless the order was refunded, canceled or failed by the time the request is due, the customer opted out, your store’s consent field says no, or the customer was asked within the cooldown. Nothing depends on what they bought, what they paid or what they might think of you.

Does Action Scheduler need WP-Cron?

Action Scheduler runs on WP-Cron and on admin page loads. On a store with little traffic, a real cron job calling wp-cron.php makes the requests go out on time.

Can I test the WooCommerce connection?

Yes: Test connection on WooCommerce > Grades.com reviews calls the Grades.com API with your key and shows the user, the business and whether review requests can be sent (plan, postal address, paused).

Is my key visible on the site?

No. The plugin sends it in an X-Grades-Key request header from your server and never prints it. A publishable key can only read your visible reviews anyway.

How often are reviews refreshed?

Every 10 minutes by default (Settings > Grades Reviews > Cache time). “Clear cached reviews” forces a refresh. The Grades API itself updates when your review sources sync.

Nothing shows up.

Visitors see nothing when the key is missing or the API is unreachable; administrators see a notice, and the page source contains an HTML comment such as <!-- grades-reviews: unavailable (http_401) -->. http_401 and http_403 mean a wrong or revoked key, http_429 means rate limiting, request_failed means your server could not reach the API.

Can the widget hide my section heading when there are no reviews yet?

Yes. Add hide_if_empty=".your-section" to [grades_widget]: when Grades.com reports that the widget has nothing to show, the plugin hides the closest element with that selector (or only the widget with hide_if_empty="1"). With CSS only: .your-section:has([data-grades-state=empty]){display:none}.

Does the block appear in the editor?

The block is server-rendered and ships without editor JavaScript. On WordPress versions that support PHP-only blocks it appears in the inserter. On older versions use the core “Shortcode” block with [grades_reviews]; the block still renders if it is already in your content or templates.

What structured data does the plugin print?

Only when you switch it on (Settings > Grades Reviews > Structured data; off by default): one JSON-LD block with your business name, your site’s URL and an aggregateRating (the rating and the number of ratings). Never a Review item, never review text and never a reviewer’s name, for any business. The figures are the true totals of exactly the business named: the key’s business, or with “Locations” exactly those locations combined, so name the business (or set the @id of your SEO plugin’s entity) that matches. For a healthcare business the same rule applies and the settings screen says so: rating and count only, no review content; leave the box unchecked to print nothing at all.

Will Google show stars in search for my own reviews?

Google decides that. Its guidelines treat reviews a business collects about itself as self-serving, and it often ignores them for LocalBusiness and Organization markup. The JSON-LD is valid and harmless, but do not expect rich result stars.

Can I turn the JSON-LD off?

Yes, it is off by default. Leave it off if your SEO plugin already outputs a rating for the same business.
sections.changelog:
1.13.0

  • New: min_cards="3" on [grades_widget] hides the widget while fewer than that many reviews qualify (1 to 10), for example on a city page that shows 4 stars and up: a widget with one or two cards can look empty. It then behaves like an empty widget, so hide_if_empty hides it and its section too. A saved widget’s own minimum cannot be lowered by the shortcode.

1.12.1

  • Visitors without JavaScript now get the “Reviews on Grades.com” link on a headquarters widget too (all locations, a set of locations, or a saved widget placed by its id): it goes to the page where those locations’ reviews are together, such as your brand page on Grades.com. Before, an HQ widget printed no link at all.

1.12.0

  • A saved widget placed by its id alone ([grades_widget widget_id="..."], no preset) now shows exactly as saved: its layout, minimum rating, count, locations and look. Attributes you add override single settings; a min_rating lower than the saved one is ignored (the saved minimum is a floor).
  • mix_locations="off" keeps the newest-first order on a headquarters widget (by default the offices take turns).

1.11.0

  • Several locations, one key: locations="all" or the ids of some locations on [grades_widget], [grades_reviews], [grades_rating], [grades_showcase], their blocks, the Elementor widget and the JSON-LD (Settings > Structured data > Locations), for a key created on a headquarters business. The rating and count are the true combined figures of exactly those locations. show_location names the office on each review. A saved showcase of any location works with the HQ key.
  • When something cannot be shown (no key, a location that is not yours, a deleted showcase), administrators now see a short note with the reason in its place, also for [grades_showcase] and [grades_widget]; visitors still see nothing.
  • Settings > Usage explains the setup for several locations and lists the review button; the Plugins screen description lists every widget.
  • JSON-LD: the rating prints with 2 decimals (no more 4.12000000000000010658…), an optional @id joins the entity of your SEO plugin, an optional additionalType, and the types MedicalBusiness and ProfessionalService. Rating and count only: never a Review item or review text (a filter that adds one is undone); the settings screen states it for a healthcare business.
  • Review cards: the head (stars, name, site, date) is now a <div> with its own font size, weight and line height, so theme rules such as article header { font-size: 1.4rem } no longer blow it up. A theme that styled .grades-review header should use .grades-review__head.

1.10.0

  • [grades_widget] reserves the widget’s height before the Grades.com script runs, so the page no longer jumps when the widget appears (the carousel, grid, list and masonry follow your column width). The iframe mode (iframe="1") is as tall as the widget too: no blank band under a carousel on desktop.
  • New: hide_if_empty="1" on [grades_widget] (and “Hide when there is nothing to show” in the block) hides the widget when Grades.com has nothing to show yet; hide_if_empty=".my-section" also hides the closest wrapper with that CSS class, for example your section heading. Themes can listen for the grades:empty event themselves.
  • Visitors without JavaScript get a “Reviews on Grades.com” link where the widget would be.
  • A review button without a review page, and other widgets with nothing to show, take no room on the page.

1.9.6

  • New: with_photo="on" on [grades_widget] together with reviewer_picture="photos": only reviews whose reviewer has a photo (where your business confirmed its reviewers’ permission on Grades.com; otherwise it is ignored). The rating and review count stay your overall figures.
  • New: card_style="gradient" (“Grades.com gradient”, also in the block and the Elementor widget): the cyan-to-purple ring of the Grades.com review badges as the card border.

1.9.5

  • New: reviewer_picture="off" (no picture) or reviewer_picture="photos" (the reviewer’s photo where your business confirmed its reviewers’ permission on Grades.com, initials for everyone else) on [grades_widget] review cards. Initials stay the default.

1.9.4

  • A business that chooses to show its own Yelp reviews on Grades.com gets them in its reviews cards word for word: a card shortens one only at the end of a sentence, never leaving out a “not” or “but”, and otherwise leaves that review out.

1.9.3

  • Security: CSS from the grades_reviews_css filter is stripped of tags (and any “<“) before it is added as inline style.
  • Security: the JSON-LD is printed with wp_print_inline_script_tag() and hex-escaped JSON.
  • Security: widget, block and Elementor output is escaped with wp_kses() right before it is printed; theme widget wrappers with wp_kses_post(); request and form values are sanitized.
  • The “add your publishable key” notice shows only on the Plugins screen and Settings > Grades Reviews (no longer on the Dashboard).
  • Readme: the review widgets loaded from Grades.com are listed under External services; Contributors is gradescom, the plugin owner account.

1.9.2

  • WooCommerce review requests: the plan texts now match Grades.com. Requests from WooCommerce count as review requests sent by hand, so they work on every paid plan (on Starter up to 50 a month, by email, without reminders); they no longer say the Premium plan is needed.

1.9.1

  • Elementor: the classic “Grades Reviews” sidebar widget no longer shows in the Elementor panel next to the new “Grades.com Reviews” widget. It still works in classic widget areas and widgets already placed there.

1.9.0

  • New: the newer Grades.com widget options on [grades_widget], the “Grades Review Widget” block and the Elementor widget: show_summary (a one-line AI summary of your reviews), controls (visitor tabs and filters: sites, stars, sort), sort (newest, highest, lowest), font (inherit, manrope, system, serif), radius (0-24), card_style (bordered, elevated, flat), star_color (hex), translate (show reviews translated into the widget language) and widget_id (a widget saved in your Grades.com dashboard, with its custom CSS). Grades.com uses them only when they are available for your business and plan; otherwise the widget looks exactly as before.

1.8.0

  • New: with Elementor active, a native “Grades.com Reviews” widget (search “Grades” in the Elementor panel). Its settings are the widget options of [grades_widget] (layout, number of reviews, lowest rating, sites, tags, colors, accent, language, rating display, caption). Inline widgets show live in the Elementor editor; floating ones (badge, pop-ups, side tab) show a note and appear on the published page. Nothing loads unless Elementor is active.
  • The Grades.com widget script is now a registered script (grades-reviews-widget), so page builders that cache their output still load it.

1.7.0

  • New: [grades_widget preset="button"], a “Leave us a review” button to your Grades.com review page (the same page for every visitor).
  • New: show_reply="on" shows your public reply under each review in the carousel, grid, list, masonry and side tab widgets.
  • New: theme="auto" follows each visitor’s light or dark setting.
  • Change: widgets now show every rating by default (newest first). min_rating still narrows them; the rating and review count next to them always stay your overall figures.
  • Change: without an accent, a widget takes the accent of your Grades.com review page.
  • Widgets load no fonts or files from anyone but Grades.com.

1.6.2

  • Fix: when Grades.com cannot be reached, a page no longer waits for every shortcode in turn (a page with four of them took over 20 seconds). The first call waits at most 3 seconds, the others are skipped for 2 minutes, and visitors keep seeing the reviews loaded last time (up to 7 days old). A revoked key still stops the reviews at once. Settings > Grades Reviews says when the saved copy is shown.
  • Fix: the “Grades Review Widget” block now shows the widget in the block editor (it was an empty block until you published). Floating widgets (badge, pop-ups, side tab) show a note saying they appear in a corner of the published page.
  • Fix: the block settings have plain names (“Lowest rating shown”, “Show dates”) instead of “MINRATING” and “showDates”. The widget block also takes review tags, like the shortcode.
  • Fix: the rating pill ([grades_widget preset="pill"]) stays inside the sentence it is placed in instead of breaking the paragraph.
  • Fix: star ratings read right where the stylesheet does not apply (feeds, reader views, strict security headers): a 3-star review shows three filled and two outline stars.
  • Fix: an admin who places a shortcode or block that matches no review now sees why (only admins, never visitors).
  • Change: Settings > Grades Reviews links to the page that creates a publishable key, lists every shortcode and block, and says plainly that the widgets carry the publishable key in the page. Pasting a secret key (gk_live_) is refused with a warning that it must never go into a website.

1.6.1

  • Fix: when your review request campaign on Grades.com is paused, WooCommerce > Grades.com reviews now says “Review requests for orders are on, but the campaign on Grades.com is paused: nothing is emailed until you resume it at my.grades.com/review-requests.” and each order note says “Grades.com review request created; the campaign is paused, so nothing is emailed until it is resumed.” instead of “sent”. The screen reads the state from Grades.com again when you open it (at most every 10 minutes) and after every save, and it says “on” only when Grades.com actually emails the requests: when review requests are paused in Grades.com, the plan does not include them, Grades.com cannot email yet or the state cannot be read, it says so instead, and the order note says nothing is emailed until that changes.
  • Fix: Yelp reviews no longer show as an empty “Anonymous” card in [grades_reviews], [grades_showcase], the classic widget and the blocks. Grades.com never sends Yelp review text to websites (rating and link only), so these reviews are left out of the cards, as are reviews without any text; they still count in [grades_rating] and the JSON-LD rating. The list asks for a few more reviews so it still fills up to your limit.
  • Fix: [grades_widget] with a publishable key limited to other websites no longer shows an empty box. Admins see why (“Grades.com refused this publishable key for this website…”) and visitors get nothing visible, like the other shortcodes.
  • Fix: [grades_reviews] shows reviewer names and review ages the same way as [grades_showcase] and the Grades.com widgets (“Jane D.”, ages counted in whole days).
  • Fix: [grades_rating] on its own line stays inside the content column of block themes such as Twenty Twenty-Five.

1.6.0

  • New: WooCommerce review requests. A completed (or processing) order queues your Grades.com review request for the billing email after a delay (default 7 days), with a per-customer cooldown (default 90 days), skips refunded and canceled orders at send time, respects Grades.com opt-outs and an optional store consent field, and never filters customers by product, order value or sentiment. Order notes, a masked event log, Test connection, a business picker and an optional “send now” action. HPOS compatible.
  • New: suggested privacy policy text and a personal data exporter and eraser for the review request data.
  • Improved: when reviews can’t be loaded, the settings page says why in plain English (revoked key, plan, rate limit, Grades.com outage, connection blocked by the host) and what to do; admins also see the reason under the shortcode, widget or block (visitors never do).
  • Fix: the review site label comes from the review platform (Yelp, Google, Facebook…) instead of the internal collector name, so a Yelp review no longer says “Yelp Apify”, and Google reviews from every collector get the same grades-source-google class. Works with older Grades.com API answers too. Templates get $review['site'] (the platform; source now holds the same value).

1.5.0

  • New: tags on [grades_widget], [grades_reviews] and [grades_showcase]: show only reviews with one of your review tags, e.g. [grades_widget preset="carousel" tags="service:roofing"] on a Roofing page. A tag with no reviews shows the widget’s empty message.

1.4.0

  • New: preset="pill", a one-line rating pill for a hero or next to a button (variant="plain" without a border, panel="on" opens a small panel of reviews). Free on a claimed Grades.com listing, with the rating strip.
  • New: display options on every widget: show_grade, show_count, show_rating, show_stars, show_rating_word (Excellent, Great, Good), show_source_mark, rating_decimals (1 or 2) and label (a short caption).

1.3.0

  • New: nine more widget layouts for [grades_widget] and the block: list, masonry, spotlight, summary (your rating with a bar per review site), wall (large reviews that scroll by themselves, for a lobby screen), video (video reviews left on Grades.com), and the floating badge, popup and tab, which sit over your page.
  • New: lang="es" (Spanish), columns, autoplay, interval, show_dates, show_site, position (left, right), mobile (pop-ups on phones) and height (the wall).

1.2.0

  • New: [grades_widget preset="strip|carousel|grid"] and the block “Grades Review Widget”: the Grades.com review widgets (a rating strip with your grade, a review carousel or a review grid), light or dark, in your accent color. They keep themselves up to date. iframe="1" for themes that strip scripts.

1.1.0

  • New: [grades_showcase] and the block “Grades Review Showcase”: your reviews picked by rules (a saved showcase from your Grades.com dashboard, or count, minimum rating, topic, sites, text length, age, language). Never shortened, with a link to all your reviews.
  • New: the showcase rules on [grades_reviews] (topic, showcase, min_length, max_length, max_age_days, language, seed) switch it to the showcase.

1.0.1

  • Fix: settings notices (bad key, missing business name) were shown twice.
  • Fix: show_date="0" now also hides the date of the owner’s response.
  • Fix: the block preview in the editor is styled (the screen-reader-only “Read more” text was visible).
  • Fix: uninstalling also removes the widget settings.

1.0.0

  • First release: settings page, [grades_reviews], [grades_rating], classic widget, server-rendered block, JSON-LD aggregateRating, transient caching.

  • Responses are cached with transients; a failing API never slows the page down for more than 5 seconds and is not retried for 2 minutes.
  • Review text and names are escaped, stars carry a text alternative, and a theme can replace the review markup with grades-reviews/review.php.

You need a Grades.com account and a publishable key (gk_pub_...). Create one in the Grades dashboard under your location’s keys.

WooCommerce review requests (1.6.0)

With WooCommerce active, WooCommerce > Grades.com reviews sends your Grades.com review request to the customer after an order is completed. Off until you switch it on.

  • Ask when an order is Completed (default) or Processing, after a delay you choose (default 7 days), through WooCommerce’s Action Scheduler.
  • One request per order, and at most one per customer every 90 days by default (Grades.com applies its own limit too and never asks again someone who already left a review after a request).
  • At send time, refunded, canceled or failed orders are skipped; optionally free orders too.
  • Customers who opted out with Grades.com are never asked. If your checkout or newsletter plugin stores marketing consent in an order or customer field, name it and the plugin respects it.
  • Every customer gets the same request: the plugin never looks at products, order value (beyond the optional free-order switch) or how happy a customer seems, asks for no rating first and offers no reward. That keeps you within Google’s review policy and the FTC rule on consumer reviews (16 CFR 465).
  • A note on each order (queued, sent, skipped and why), a log of the last 50 events with masked emails, and an optional “Send review request now” order action (off by default).
  • Works on every paid Grades.com plan (on Starter up to 50 review requests a month, by email, without reminders) and needs a secret API key (gk_live_..., scopes reviews:read, reviews:write, companies:read), created at https://my.grades.com/connect?connect=woocommerce. The key is stored with autoload off, sent only from your server and never shown again.
  • HPOS (custom order tables) compatible; orders are read and written through the WooCommerce order API.

Shortcode: reviews

[grades_reviews limit="6" min_rating="4" sources="google,yelp" sort="best" layout="grid" show_source="1" show_date="1"]
  • limit 1-50, default 6
  • min_rating 1-5, default from Settings
  • sources comma separated, default from Settings (empty = all)
  • sort newest (default) or best
  • layout grid (default) or list
  • show_source, show_date 1 or 0
  • max_chars characters shown before “Read more”, default 280
  • locations (a key created on a headquarters business) all or location ids, comma separated; default: the key’s own business
  • show_location 1 puts the office on each review (with locations)

Shortcode: rating

[grades_rating] or `[grades_rating sources="google" stars="0"]` or `[grades_rating locations="all"]`

Several locations on one site (1.11.0)

Create ONE publishable key on your headquarters (HQ) business at my.grades.com and paste it in Settings > Grades Reviews. Then:

  • Home page or reviews page: [grades_widget preset="carousel" locations="all"], [grades_rating locations="all"]: every location, with the true combined rating and count.
  • A city page: [grades_widget preset="grid" locations="<id>,<id>"] (the location ids are listed in the widget editor’s “Which reviews” step at my.grades.com), or a widget saved at my.grades.com with its own choice of locations: [grades_widget widget_id="<saved widget id>"].
  • A saved showcase of any of your locations works with the HQ key: [grades_showcase showcase="<id>"].
  • show_location="on" (widgets) or show_location="1" ([grades_reviews], [grades_showcase]) names the office on each review.

Without locations, [grades_reviews], [grades_rating], [grades_showcase] and the JSON-LD show the key’s own business (as before 1.11.0), while a widget on an HQ key shows all locations by default (as on Grades.com). If Grades.com refuses a value (a location that is not yours), administrators see a short note with the reason where the reviews would be; visitors see nothing.

Theme override

Create grades-reviews/review.php in your theme. It receives $review (author, rating, site (the review platform: google, yelp, facebook…), source (the same), source_label, text, excerpt, truncated, date, url, response_text, response_date; all text is plain, escape it when printing) and $args.

External services

This plugin calls the Grades.com public reviews API (https://app.grades.com/api/v1/public/reviews, /public/summary and /public/showcase; the base URL is configurable) from your web server to fetch your reviews and rating summary. It sends your publishable key (header X-Grades-Key), the filter values of the shortcode (limit, sort, minimum rating, sources, locations, and the showcase rules: showcase id, count, topic, text length, age, language) and a User-Agent containing the plugin version and your site URL. Nothing about your visitors is sent from your server.

The optional review widgets ([grades_widget], the “Grades Review Widget” block and the Elementor “Grades.com Reviews” widget) are loaded in your visitors’ browsers from Grades.com: the script https://app.grades.com/embed/widget.js, or a frame from https://app.grades.com/embed/widget/... with iframe="1" and in the editor preview. The page carries your publishable key and the widget options (layout, filters, colors, language, the locations of a headquarters key, a saved widget id). As with any web request, the visitor’s browser sends Grades.com its IP address, browser user agent and the page address (frames send only your site’s origin). The widget sets no cookie. Nothing loads from Grades.com in your visitors’ browsers unless you place a widget. Terms of use: https://www.grades.com/terms. Privacy policy: https://www.grades.com/privacy-policy.

With WooCommerce and the review requests switched on (WooCommerce > Grades.com reviews), the plugin also calls the authenticated Grades.com API v1 (https://app.grades.com/api/v1, same configurable base URL) from your web server with your secret key (header Authorization: Bearer): /me, /companies and /companies/{business}/review-requests/settings when you save the settings, press Test connection, or open that settings screen more than 10 minutes after the last check, and POST /companies/{business}/review-requests once per eligible order, when the request is due. For each order it sends the customer’s billing name and billing email, an order reference made of a hash of your site address and the order id, the consent source “woocommerce_order”, and the plugin version and site URL in the User-Agent. Grades.com then emails the customer your review request with an unsubscribe link. Nothing is sent for orders while the feature is off. Service: Grades.com, https://www.grades.com/integrations/wordpress. Terms of use: https://www.grades.com/terms. Privacy policy: https://www.grades.com/privacy-policy.
